summary: This pair had 442 FDR-significant downstream genes with HSP/proteasome/apoptotic induction, including Hsp90aa1, Ubc, Psmc3, Psmc4, Bax, Hspa1a/b, and Hsph1, plus reduced neuronal genes including Slc17a7, Grm7, Thy1, Dnm1, and Gria2. Psmc1 deletion is documented to deplete neuronal 26S proteasomes and proteasome insufficiency is documented to induce Nrf1 proteasome bounce-back with heat-shock, ER-stress, and apoptotic programs, predicting the observed positive stress/proteasome direction.

The only FDR-supported downstream changes were Ahi1 down and Pafah1b2/Nbdy up. Pair-specific searches for a Psmc1/Rpt2 relationship to Ahi1, Pafah1b2, or Nbdy, and for a broader proteasome-stress route to this sparse three-gene pattern, found no direct or biologically specific partial bridge.

cell_type: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
summary: The 433-gene response combined Dnajb4, Psmc3/Psmc4, Psmd1/Psmd9/Psme4, Ddit3, HSPs, Aen, and Ccng1 induction with Dnm1 and Camk2a/Camk2b reduction. The literature predicts that Psmc1 loss should compromise neuronal 26S proteasomes and that proteasome insufficiency should increase proteasome-subunit and proteotoxic-stress transcripts, matching the central positive response module.

This barely eligible pair had Psmc4 up and Entr1 down as the only significant non-target genes. Nrf1-mediated proteasome bounce-back specifically predicts increased proteasome subunit transcription when proteasome activity is compromised, so the Psmc4 direction agrees; no target-specific literature bridge was found for the concurrent Entr1 decrease.

The significant 10-gene response was mostly positive and led by Hgs, Zfp654, Ubc, Uchl1, and BC005537, with Syt7 as the only down-regulated hit. Searches for Psmc1/Rpt2 connections to Hgs, Ubc, Uchl1, BC005537, or Syt7 did not find a specific target-to-module relationship; UPS membership of Ubc and Uchl1 alone was not treated as a pair-level mechanistic bridge.

CTX-CGE GABA cells had a 131-gene mixed response with Atp6v0c, Thy1, Grin2b, and Syp down, BC005537 and Uchl1 up, and only weak Bax induction. Neuronal Psmc1 loss is documented to impair 26S proteasomes and produce neurodegeneration, but the literature did not directly connect that injury phenotype to this CGE GABA transcript pattern or directionally predict the BC005537/Uchl1 component.

The Pvalb GABA response included up-regulated Psmc3, Psmd3, Psmd1, Psme4, Usp5, Uchl1, Dnajb4, and Hgs and down-regulated Snrpn, Vamp1, Scn1a, and Kifc2. Psmc1-dependent loss of neuronal 26S proteasome function plus the Nrf1 proteasome bounce-back pathway predict increased proteasome machinery transcripts, which is the clearest directional module in this pair.

CNU-MGE GABA cells showed 107 FDR-significant genes, including Psmd1/Psme4/Psmd3 and Usp5 induction, Ddit3/Bax/Ccng1 induction, and Atp1a3, Dnm1, and Syp reduction. The documented consequence of Psmc1 loss is neuronal 26S proteasome impairment, and proteasome insufficiency predicts compensatory proteasome-subunit and proteotoxic-stress induction in the observed direction.

The pair was eligible on a single downstream gene, Rnpc3 down-regulation. Searches for Psmc1/Rpt2 with Rnpc3 or for a Psmc1 proteasome-stress mechanism that specifically predicts lower Rnpc3 did not identify a direct or partial target-to-response bridge.

The CNU-HYa/HY GABA response had 1,351 downstream hits, with Psmc3, Psmc6, Psmd1, Psme4, Hsp90aa1/Hsp90ab1, Hspa1a/b, Hsph1, Ddit3, Bax, Mdm2, Ccng1, and Aen induced and neuronal markers such as Dnm1 and Atp1a3 reduced. Psmc1 loss is known to compromise neuronal 26S proteasomes, and the Nrf1/HSP/ER-stress literature predicts positive proteasome and proteotoxic-stress responses after proteasome insufficiency.

The 1,057-gene CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic response was centered on induction of Bax, Hsp90ab1, Psme4, Ubc, Ddit3, Psmd3, Psmc6, Psmc4, Psmd1, Mdm2, Ccng1, Hspa1a, Hsph1, and Dnajb4. That direction matches target-specific Psmc1 neuronal proteasome loss and the documented transcriptional reaction to proteasome inhibition: proteasome-subunit bounce-back plus HSP, UPR, and pro-apoptotic induction.

MH-LH/TH glutamatergic cells had 290 downstream FDR hits, with Clu, Psmd3, Psmc6, Ubc, Ddit3, Bax, Hsph1, Psme4, and HSP90 genes induced while Atp1a3 and Slc17a6 were reduced. Psmc1 loss is expected to reduce 26S proteasome function, and the literature predicts compensatory proteasome-gene and proteotoxic-stress induction, matching the central observed module.

The TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic response included 656 significant genes and a positive proteostasis/stress module containing Psmd1, Psmc6, Psmc3, Psmc4, Ddit3, Zfand2a, Dnajb4, Hsph1, Bax, Ccng1, and Ubc. Psmc1-dependent proteasome depletion and the Nrf1/HSP/ER-stress response to proteasome insufficiency together predict this induction direction.

Midbrain glutamatergic cells had 3,622 downstream hits, with strong Hsph1, Hsp90aa1/Hsp90ab1, Hspa1a/b, Dnajb1/Dnajb4, Ddit3, Bax, Mdm2, Ccng1, Psmc3/Psmc4/Psmc6, Psmd1/Psmd3/Psmd9, Psme4, and Ubc induction and neuronal-channel/synaptic loss. The documented Psmc1-to-26S-proteasome relationship plus proteasome-insufficiency bounce-back and proteotoxic-stress programs directly predict the induced module.

The 2,772-gene midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA response paired loss of Scn1a, Atp1a3, Gria2, Thy1, Atp1b1, Syp, and Vamp1 with strong Bax, Hsp90aa1/Hsp90ab1, Psmc3/Psmc4/Psmc6, Psmd1/Psmd3, Psme4, Ddit3, Mdm2, Ccng1, Dnajb1, Hsph1, Ubc, and Hspa1a/b induction. Published Psmc1 neuronal deletion and proteasome-inhibition studies predict the proteasome-stress and apoptotic induction direction, so the central module agrees.

Cerebellar GABA cells had a 56-gene response with Psmc6, Psme4, Psmd9, Zfand2a, Ccng1, and Mdm2 induced and Snrpn, Atp1a3, Atp1b1, Bcan, and Sv2a reduced. The up-regulated proteasome subunits and stress/apoptotic markers follow the documented response to 26S proteasome compromise downstream of Psmc1 loss.
